note: Wren Phonics mnemonic character renames (Ealing review, 2026-10-13). Each new name (and, where possible, the animal or object) starts with or clearly contains the SOUND being taught, never the letter name. STAGED, NOT APPLIED: apply with scripts/phonics/apply-mnemonic-rename.js only after the new pictures exist and Toby has approved the picks.

old.name: Acer
old.mnemonic: Acer the acorn drops from the branch and bounces on the ground three times — 'a, a, a'!
old.action: Crouch down and spring up a tiny bit three times, like Acer bouncing on the ground, saying 'a, a, a'.

character.name: Annie
character.blurb: Annie is a busy little ant who taps her feelers on everything she finds.

new.mnemonic: Annie the ant taps her feelers on a crumb — 'a, a, a'!
new.action: Tap two fingers together three times like Annie's feelers, saying 'a, a, a'.

renames.reason: Acer and acorn both start with the letter NAME /ay/, not the short /a/ being taught. Annie and ant both start with /a/ (as in apple, the cue picture).
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon ant character, shiny red-brown body in three round parts, six thin legs, two bent antennae with little round tips, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, standing, three-quarter view

old.name: Gigi
old.mnemonic: Gigi the egg wobbles gently from side to side — 'g, g, g' — rocking but never falling.
old.action: Rock gently from side to side on the spot, like Gigi wobbling in her nest, saying 'g, g'.

character.name: Gus
character.blurb: Gus is a cheerful little goat who gulps his grass in one go.

new.mnemonic: Gus the goat gulps down his grass — 'g, g, g'.
new.action: Put a hand on your throat and do three little gulps like Gus, saying 'g, g, g'.

renames.reason: Gigi is often said with a soft g (/zh/ or /j/) and the motif was an egg (/e/). Gus and goat both start with hard /g/; goat is already the cue picture for g.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon baby goat character, white and light brown coat, two short curved horns, a little beard tuft under the chin, four hooves, short upright tail, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, standing, three-quarter view

old.name: Ozzy
old.mnemonic: Ozzy the owl opens his big round eyes wide and hoots — 'o, o, o'.
old.action: Make two round circles with your thumbs and fingers and hold them up to your eyes like Ozzy's, saying 'o, o'.

character.name: Ozzy
character.blurb: Ozzy is a playful otter who pops his head out of the river to look around.

new.mnemonic: Ozzy the otter pops up out of the river and opens his mouth wide — 'o, o, o'.
new.action: Make a round O with your mouth and pop up from a crouch like Ozzy, saying 'o, o'.

renames.reason: Ozzy starts with /o/, but the motif was an owl, which starts with /ow/. Ozzy the otter: both start with short /o/.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon river otter character, sleek brown fur with a cream face and tummy, small round ears, long thick tail, webbed paws, whiskers, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, standing on hind legs, three-quarter view

old.name: Una
old.mnemonic: Una the butterfly dips down low, then lifts up, up, up into the air — 'u, u, u'.
old.action: Scoop both hands from your waist up to your shoulders, like Una lifting off, saying a short 'u'.

character.name: Umber
character.blurb: Umber is a little brown bug who loves to climb up, up, up a tall stem.

new.mnemonic: Umber the bug climbs up, up, up the stem — 'u, u, u'.
new.action: Walk two fingers up your arm like Umber climbing, saying a short 'u' each step.

renames.reason: Una starts with /yoo/, the letter name. Umber starts with the short /u/ being taught, and bug has the same sound.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon beetle-like bug character, round warm brown shell with a few darker spots, six short legs, two short antennae, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, standing, three-quarter view

old.name: Vela
old.mnemonic: Vela the vole feels her whiskers vibrate, vvv, whenever she trundles her tiny cart of seeds.
old.action: Rest two fingers lightly on your chin and let them 'buzz' while you hum vvv.

character.name: Vela
character.blurb: Vela is a little vole who pulls a cart of seeds, whiskers buzzing as the wheels turn.

renames.reason: Name and mnemonic were right (Vela the vole), but the character record said hedgehog, so the picture drawn from it would not match the words. Motif corrected to vole.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon field vole character, round body with soft grey-brown fur, small round ears, short tail, tiny pink paws, long whiskers, pulling a tiny wooden cart of seeds, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, three-quarter view

old.name: Xander
old.mnemonic: Xander the fox crosses his front paws, ks-ks, when he's about to pounce.
old.action: Cross your arms in front of your chest like an X while saying ks-ks.

character.name: Max
character.blurb: Max is a cheeky little fox who crosses his paws before he pounces.

new.mnemonic: Max the fox crosses his front paws, ks-ks, when he's about to pounce.

renames.reason: Xander starts with /z/, but x is taught as /ks/, a sound that comes at the END of English words. Max and fox both end in /ks/ (DfE: 'x' as /k+s/ in 'box'). The record also said hedgehog; corrected to fox.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon fox cub character, bright orange fur, white chest and white tip on a big bushy tail, pointed ears with dark tips, black paws, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, sitting with front paws crossed, three-quarter view

old.name: Nigel
old.mnemonic: Nigel the nest hums a long, low ng-ng note that wobbles the twigs around him.
old.action: Hum ng-ng with your mouth slightly open and the back of your tongue raised, and tap your nose gently to feel it buzz.

character.name: King
character.blurb: King is a bright little kingfisher who hums a long, low ng while he waits by the river.

new.mnemonic: King the kingfisher hums a long, low ng-ng while he waits on his branch by the river.

renames.reason: Nigel starts with /n/, but ng (/ng/) never starts an English word; the anchor must end in it. King and kingfisher both contain /ng/.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon kingfisher bird character, bright blue back and wings, orange chest, long pointed dark beak, small red feet, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, perched on a twig, three-quarter view

old.name: Ellie
old.mnemonic: Ellie the owl stretches up tall on her branch to see far and wide, ee-ee.
old.action: Stretch your neck up tall, hands framing wide eyes, and hold ee-ee for a full breath.

character.name: Keeley
character.blurb: Keeley is a fluffy little sheep who stretches up tall to peep over the hedge.

new.mnemonic: Keeley the sheep stretches up tall to peep over the hedge — ee-ee.
new.action: Stretch your neck up tall, hands framing wide eyes like Keeley peeping, and hold ee-ee for a full breath.

renames.reason: Ellie starts with short /e/, not the long /ee/ being taught. Keeley and sheep both have /ee/ spelt ee.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon lamb character, round fluffy white wool body, dark grey face and legs, small floppy ears, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, standing, three-quarter view

old.name: Otto
old.mnemonic: Otto the duckling floats along, round and steady, oa-oa, wherever the pond takes him.
old.action: Round your lips into an O, rock gently side to side like floating, and say oa-oa.

character.name: Oakley
character.blurb: Oakley is a calm little toad who floats on a lily pad, round and steady.

new.mnemonic: Oakley the toad floats on his lily pad, round and steady — oa-oa.
new.action: Round your lips into an O, rock gently side to side like Oakley floating, and say oa-oa.

renames.reason: Otto starts with short /o/, not /oa/. Oakley starts with /oa/ spelt oa, and toad has the same sound and spelling.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon toad character, round bumpy olive-green body with a pale tummy, wide smiling mouth, webbed feet, big golden friendly shiny eyes, full body, sitting on a round green lily pad, three-quarter view

old.name: Bobbin
old.mnemonic: Bobbin the hedgehog gives a quick, soft puff, oo-oo, when he's pushing a heavy pinecone.
old.action: Give a quick, soft puff of breath, oo-oo, like you're pushing something heavy just twice.

character.name: Woody
character.blurb: Woody is a busy little woodpecker who taps short, quick taps on the wood.

new.mnemonic: Woody the woodpecker taps quick, short taps on the wood — oo, oo.
new.action: Tap a finger quickly on the table, twice, like Woody, saying a short oo, oo.

renames.reason: Bobbin has no short /oo/ in it at all. Woody and woodpecker both have the short /oo/ of book, spelt oo.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon woodpecker bird character, black and white wings, a bright red patch on the head, a strong straight pointed beak, short stiff tail, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, clinging to a tree trunk, three-quarter view

old.name: Otis
old.mnemonic: Otis the owl flaps out and hoots a loud, surprised ow-ow when a branch wobbles under him.
old.action: Throw both arms out wide as if wobbling off balance and yelp ow-ow.

character.name: Howie
character.blurb: Howie is an owl who gives a startled ow-ow whenever his branch wobbles.

new.mnemonic: Howie the owl flaps out and hoots a loud, surprised ow-ow when a branch wobbles under him.

renames.reason: Otis starts with the /oa/ sound, the wrong one for ow (as in cow). Howie and owl both have /ow/; owl is even spelt ow.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon owl character, round coral-brown feathered body, two pointed ear tufts, big round friendly shiny eyes, small hooked beak, full body, standing on a branch, three-quarter view

old.name: Oskar
old.mnemonic: Oskar the caterpillar bumps into a shiny leaf and calls out a sharp oi-oi in surprise.
old.action: Throw one hand up like calling out to a friend and say a sharp oi-oi.

character.name: Oink
character.blurb: Oink is a little piglet who calls out oi! whenever something surprises her.

new.mnemonic: Oink the piglet bumps into a shiny leaf and calls out a sharp oi-oi in surprise.

renames.reason: Oskar starts with short /o/. Oink starts with /oi/ spelt oi.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon piglet character, round pink body, curly tail, small pointed ears, round snout, four little trotters, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, standing, three-quarter view

old.name: Edie
old.mnemonic: Edie the sparrow leans in close and tilts her head, ear-ear, whenever a sound is far away.
old.action: Cup a hand behind your ear and lean your head in gently, saying ear-ear.

character.name: Kiera
character.blurb: Kiera is a shy little earwig who tilts her head to listen for faraway sounds.

new.mnemonic: Kiera the earwig leans in close and tilts her head, ear-ear, whenever a sound is far away.

renames.reason: Edie starts with /ee/, not /ear/. Earwig starts with /ear/ spelt ear, and Kiera has the same sound.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon earwig insect character, long slim shiny chestnut-brown body, six thin legs, two long antennae, a pair of small curved pincers at the tail end, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, three-quarter view

old.name: Amara
old.mnemonic: Amara the feather drifts on the breeze, floating and swaying, air-air, before it lands.
old.action: Hold one hand up like a feather and let it drift side to side slowly through the air, saying air-air.

character.name: Airlie
character.blurb: Airlie is a quick little hare who leaps high into the air.

new.mnemonic: Airlie the hare leaps high into the air — air, air — before she lands.
new.action: Hold one hand up and let it leap and drift slowly down like Airlie, saying air-air.

renames.reason: Amara starts with /a/ or /uh/, not /air/. Airlie starts with /air/ spelt air, and hare has the same sound.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon hare character, sandy-brown fur, very long upright ears with black tips, long back legs, white fluffy tail, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, mid-leap, three-quarter view

old.name: Ursa
old.mnemonic: Ursa the snail tucks in sure and steady, ure-ure, whenever her shell feels safe and snug.
old.action: Wrap your arms around yourself in a snug hug and hum ure-ure.

character.name: Surefoot
character.blurb: Surefoot is a careful snail who only moves when she is sure it is safe.

new.mnemonic: Surefoot the snail tucks in sure and steady, ure-ure, whenever her shell feels safe and snug.

renames.reason: Ursa starts with /ur/, a different sound. Surefoot has /ure/ spelt ure, as in sure.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon garden snail character, teal and cream swirly shell, soft pale body, two eye stalks, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, three-quarter view

old.name: Ember
old.mnemonic: Ember the mushroom mutters a soft, quiet er-er whenever a raindrop taps her cap.
old.action: Shrug your shoulders lightly and mutter a soft, quick er-er.

character.name: Jasper
character.blurb: Jasper is a quiet little spider who mutters a soft er-er as he spins.

new.mnemonic: Jasper the spider mutters a soft, quiet er-er as he spins his web.

renames.reason: Ember starts with short /e/. er is taught as the soft sound at the end of hammer; Jasper and spider both end in it, spelt er.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon spider character, round fuzzy dark body, eight thin bendy legs, big friendly shiny eyes, a tiny smile, full body, hanging from a single silk thread, three-quarter view

old.name: Echo Star
old.mnemonic: Echo Star sits at the far end of the word and can't shout her own name — instead she beams her light back over the consonant in between to wake up the 'a' and make it say its own name, 'ay'.
old.action: Children point to an imaginary letter far ahead, then mime a beam travelling backward from their fingertip to their other hand, saying 'ay' as it arrives.

character.name: Kate
character.blurb: Kate is a long, friendly snake who curls round the letter in the middle.

new.mnemonic: Kate the snake curls round the letter in the middle: the a and the e hold hands across it, and the a says /ai/, as in cake and snake.
new.action: Children hold their two hands apart, then join them in a curve over an imaginary letter, saying 'ai'.

renames.reason: Echo starts with short /e/, and the mnemonic said the a 'says its own name', which is letter-name language. Kate and snake both have /ai/ spelt a-e.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon snake character, long golden-yellow body with soft orange stripes, curled into an S shape, round head, big friendly shiny eyes, a tiny smile, three-quarter view

old.name: Hollow the Nest
old.mnemonic: Hollow the Nest sits snug at the end of the word, and she calls softly back over the consonant so the 'o' at the front says its own name, 'oh', like calling everyone home.
old.action: Children cup both hands together like a little nest, then slowly pull them apart while saying 'oh', as if opening the nest to let the sound out.

character.name: Rose
character.blurb: Rose is a little mole who digs her way home.

new.mnemonic: Rose the mole digs her way home: the o and the e hold hands across the letter in the middle, and the o says /oa/, as in home and mole.
new.action: Children cup both hands like a little mole's paws and make a digging movement, saying 'oa'.

renames.reason: Hollow starts with short /o/. Rose and mole both have /oa/ spelt o-e.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon mole character, soft dark grey velvety fur, pink pointed nose, big pink digging paws, tiny eyes made friendly and shiny, full body, peeping out of a small mound of earth, three-quarter view

old.name: Una the Owl
old.mnemonic: Una the Owl perches right at the front of a word and turns its meaning the opposite way round.
old.action: Cross both arms into an X in front of your chest, then snap them open, to show 'the opposite'.

character.name: Unwin the Owl
character.blurb: A wise owl who can turn his head almost all the way round, always ready to flip things the opposite way.

new.mnemonic: Unwin the Owl perches right at the front of a word and turns its meaning the opposite way round.

renames.reason: Una starts with /yoo/. un- says /un/, and Unwin starts with it.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon owl character, teal and cream feathers, round face with big round friendly shiny eyes, head turned to look over his shoulder, full body, perched, three-quarter view

old.name: Ess the Seed-Pip
old.mnemonic: Ess the Seed-Pip lands on the end of a word to show there's more than one, or that it's happening right now — listen for his soft hiss or buzz.
old.action: Wiggle one finger, then suddenly flash all five, to show 'one becomes many'.

character.name: Sid the Seed
character.blurb: A tiny seed who hops onto the end of words, landing so softly he only ever adds a hiss or a buzz, never a whole new word.

new.mnemonic: Sid the Seed lands on the end of a word to show there's more than one, or that it's happening right now — listen for his soft hiss or buzz.

renames.reason: 'Ess' is the letter name, not the sound. Sid starts with /s/.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon seed character, plump teardrop-shaped sage-green seed with a tiny sprout on top, two little arms, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, three-quarter view

old.name: Ezra the Bee
old.mnemonic: Ezra the Bee always adds his own buzzing beat — '-es' — onto words that already end in a hiss, like box or bus.
old.action: Cup a hand behind your ear and add a little extra nod, as if catching the extra beat.

character.name: Izzy the Bee
character.blurb: A busy bee who buzzes in with an extra beat whenever a word already ends in a hiss, so we can hear the ending properly.

new.mnemonic: Izzy the Bee always adds her own buzzing beat — '-es' — onto words that already end in a hiss, like box or bus.

renames.reason: -es says /iz/ (boxes). Ezra starts with /ez/; Izzy starts with /iz/.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon bumblebee character, round fuzzy yellow and black striped body, small clear wings, two short antennae, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, flying, three-quarter view

old.name: Eddy the Snail
old.mnemonic: Eddy the Snail leaves his trail behind him — add '-ed' to show something already happened.
old.action: Point back over your shoulder with your thumb, to show the action is already behind you.

character.name: Ted the Snail
character.blurb: A slow, thoughtful snail who always leaves a shiny trail behind him, showing where he has already been.

new.mnemonic: Ted the Snail leaves his trail behind him — add '-ed' to show something already happened. Listen: it can say /t/ (jumped), /d/ (played) or /id/ (landed).

renames.reason: -ed is never said /ed/ as in Eddy: it says /t/, /d/ or /id/. Ted has the /t/ and the /d/.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon garden snail character, plum-purple swirly shell, pale body, two eye stalks, a shiny trail behind him, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, three-quarter view

old.name: Erno the Acorn
old.mnemonic: Erno the Acorn loves comparing — add '-er' to say one thing is more than another, or to name someone who does something.
old.action: Stand on tiptoes and stretch one hand a little higher than the other.

character.name: Piper the Acorn
character.blurb: A proud little acorn who's always comparing himself to the acorn next to him, hoping to grow just a bit bigger.

new.mnemonic: Piper the Acorn loves comparing — add '-er' to say one thing is more than another, or to name someone who does something.

renames.reason: -er says the soft /uh/ at the end of faster. Erno starts with /ur/; Piper ends in the right sound.
renames.art_subject: a small friendly cartoon acorn character, smooth sandy-brown nut with a textured cap, two little arms, standing on tiptoe, big friendly shiny eyes, full body, three-quarter view
